title: Cause Analysis
text: “You can find some pretty decent-quality materials too, right? Like oreicalcum ore, or geodes.”
“I’ve been putting the ones I don’t need into my weapon, but should I be bringing them back instead?”
“Who knows. Also, the ground just cleanly vanishes whenever Motoyasu-san digs, so you can really tell it’s a dungeon gimmick.”
“It feels like we’re all adventuring together, which is pretty fun.”
“It wouldn’t be so bad if it weren’t for this appearance, I think.”
“The real drawback is that since everything’s so thoroughly reinforced, there’s hardly any challenge. The occasional gimmick requirement is just annoying, and… huh, some weird part just turned up.”
Yet another model kit part turned up partway through my digging, I say. Incidentally, I cracked open the geodes by feel to check their contents. Mostly fish-like fossils, it seemed.
“There’s more coming out too… a crystal skull, a golden airplane… once you get several of them, it stops feeling special.”
“What exactly is this?”
Itsuki asked, picking up a skull made of crystal, I say. Incidentally, there were variations—human versions, demi-human versions, and so on.
“Huh? Itsuki, you don’t know about out-of-place artifacts?”
“I feel like I’ve seen something like it in games or whatever, but I don’t know the details of where it actually comes from.”
“Same here.”
“Well… categorically speaking it’s occult stuff, so I figured in Itsuki’s world it’d probably have been thoroughly debunked by now.”
“I don’t know absolutely everything, you know.”
“These are Out-of-Place Artifacts, I say. One of those things alongside the Nazca Lines and whatnot. Though I’d wager every single one of these is a fake, I say.”
I once happened to know a pig who was an occult enthusiast, you see. It rattled off explanations at incredible speed, so I remember it well, I say.
“Motoyasu-kun, you know a lot about this stuff?”
“I have a vague memory of getting tangled up in some strange incident related to this sort of thing… or maybe I don’t. It’s hazy, I say.”
“Which is it…”
“There’s simply too much for me to remember it all, I say.”
“Well, assuming these kinds of items really existed, stories do get built around that premise sometimes. Maybe in your world, Motoyasu-kun, some of them are real.”
“Isn’t that more likely to be Itsuki’s world?”
“True enough… there’s probably some superpowered battle over the fate of the world happening around that stuff.”
At my exchange with Father, Itsuki furrowed his brow, and Ren, for some reason, took a step back from him.
“Ugh, I don’t like that… some battle happening without my knowledge, and if evil wins the world gets destroyed…”
“Don’t go imagining the secret underbelly of my world and then distancing yourself from me. Besides, didn’t we ourselves fight a battle for the fate of the world?”
“Well put. Though I suppose it wasn’t exactly us—it was other versions of us, along with Motoyasu-kun, who did the fighting.”

Father’s words carried a certain weight, his voice sounding as though he were looking off at something distant, I say. Anyway, we kept digging onward, and at the end of the path we found, we encountered and defeated a boss. The boss we fought this time somehow reminded me of the one we’d fought in whichever nation we’d been assigned to after grinding levels on Cal Mira Island. It was a Dimensional Ice Wolf, a large ice-attribute wolf monster, I say. A monster even I could have defeated back in those days—a boss monster I recognized from my game knowledge.
“Yeah, we really did take that down easily, huh~”
“I’ve pretty much memorized the dungeon layout by now. With how reinforced we all are, we shouldn’t need to spend much time on it.”
“The rest just depends on the gimmicks along the way, I guess.”
“That’s right. They’re mostly illusions, but the island-specific monsters with ‘Karma’ in their names still keep showing up as always.”
“Penguu and Peckle and all that… it’s got this ‘what they end up becoming’ vibe that I really don’t like. And processing the island-exclusive drop equipment changes you too.”
“Naofumi-san, please don’t say things this unpleasant that rival my accuracy stat. In my case, would that be Karma Squirrel?”
“Mine would be Karma Dog, I suppose.”
“Karma Rabbit for me, I say. Pitch black, it is.”
“So I’d be Karma Penguu, huh? Sounds like eating meals in the middle of the night would trigger the transformation. Would Itsuki multiply in water?”
Mass-produced Itsukis? That’s rather unsettling, I say.
“Where do you even come up with this stuff… your otaku knowledge outstrips our game knowledge, honestly.”
“From what I heard from Motoyasu and Gaelion, there’s a whole series of cursed weapons sealed inside weapons, so maybe if you dabble in that sort of thing, you end up like that?”
“That sounds plausible. It’s got an obviously evil look to it. I have a bad feeling it’ll show up as a boss somewhere.”
“Is there nothing like that among the bosses in your game knowledge?”
“Was there anything like that in your game, Ren-san?”
“Nope. The bosses you find on islands are about the limit.”
“Same for me, I say.”
After all, it was only at high-efficiency EXP events like Cal Mira Island that we’d farmed experience by defeating monsters from the Karma series.
“Still, it’s a little exciting, isn’t it? Even if none of us would ever actually end up looking like that.”
“I figure there’d be some obvious boss like a Karma King… but I already know the boss on the top floor. Abend Great D, a dragon with wings made of swords.”
“My knowledge has something similar too, just under a different name.”
“Same here, I say.”
“Well then, I guess that’s what’ll show up around there. Let’s keep pushing forward.”
And so we advanced further. The Fluffy Exploration Squad’s adventure continued, I say.
“About that chat we had earlier—there’s the other possibility that we exist too, but since we can’t observe parallel worlds ourselves, it’s beyond our comprehension, really.”
“Ren, Itsuki, don’t you two ever want to loop, like Motoyasu-kun does?”
“Even if I did, at most I’d loop a few times to build an ideal world and then break out of the loop. Though in stories, that sort of thing rarely goes well.”
“True enough. In the end, we still don’t even know why Motoyasu-kun is looping in the first place.”
Come to think of it, it really is a mystery, I say. But I simply keep fighting for Father and Filo-tan’s sake, that’s all.

“It’d be convenient if we could loop too, but then again, that would reset all our relationships, which sounds pretty rough. If we could loop together it’d be a bit easier, but… I don’t have much confidence I could get along with Sadeena-san or Lars-san again after meeting them all over from scratch.”
“No, I think Father gets along quite frequently with Older Sister and Panda regardless, I say?”
After all, even Father in the very first world had become drinking buddies with Panda. He’d gotten along well with Older Sister too.

“There’s a difference between meeting someone again without knowing it and meeting them again while knowing it. It’s the same as Motoyasu-kun not being able to meet that girl, Filo. She’s Sakura-chan, after all.”
Ugh… that struck a nerve, I say. Come to think of it, right now I’m not even in a position where I get to choose between Sakura-chan and Filo-tan in a loop.
“In stories, it’s usually the protagonist, or maybe a select few—say, the mastermind—who loop together, that’s the standard setup.”
“Ha! In other words, if I kill Rival, my loop will end, I say!”
Curse Rival! Being the mastermind behind it all, tricking me and forcing me to loop over and over again!
“Whoa, hold on, jumping to conclusions like that is premature. Besides, if Gaelion-chan really were the mastermind, wouldn’t she stop looping the moment she and I became mutually in love?”
“That’s certainly true, isn’t it.”
“Right. I think I’d stop there myself. Gaelion, who was so obsessively attached to Naofumi, calmed down that much after all.”

Gah… Father, who gave himself over to Rival—could it be that my loop might have ended right there? Where does the truth lie, I wonder? …Faintly, I recalled Father’s face as he said his farewell in the final moment of my previous loop. That had been a continuation of that very loop, hadn’t it.
『Do you… want to see him? That… that other me?』
Ngh… remembering that voice again gives me a headache, I say.

“Gaelion-san’s goal was Naofumi-san after all, so if a successful loop had been constructed, she’d stop, wouldn’t she. And even supposing Motoyasu-san wished for the loop and it happened, this time she’d surely be the one trying to make Motoyasu-san stop instead.”
